items.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra for Coding and Computer Use
items.summary_1line: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, a new model focused on coding, computer use, long-running agentic tasks, and cybersecurity, with availability across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API. By Daniel Dominguez
items.editor_note: InfoQ's report confirms availability across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API the day after launch.

items.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
items.summary_1line: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
items.editor_note: Perplexity's case study: Astra writes communications, changes software, and monitors production with fewer human check-ins.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra Is the First Model OpenAI Classifies as Critical for Cybersecurity
items.summary_1line: OpenAI has classified GPT-6 Astra at the Critical cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework, a first. In expert-led testing the model found previously unknown vulnerabilities in a browser and an OS kern...
items.editor_note: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework rates Astra Critical for cybersecurity after expert testers found real browser and OS-kernel vulnerabilities.

items.title: Higgsfield AI ships new video features in a day with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary_1line: With GPT-6 Astra, Higgsfield AI makes video ad creation easier for small businesses and brings new creative tools to market faster.
items.editor_note: Higgsfield AI's case study: new video ad-creation features shipped in a day, four days after the Critical classification.

items.title: Harvey turns legal context into stronger drafts with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary_1line: GPT-6 Astra produces more structured, context-aware legal documents, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy.
items.editor_note: Harvey's case study: Astra turns legal case context into stronger, more structured drafts, freeing lawyers for strategy work.

items.title: Basis completes a tax workbook 2x faster with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary_1line: GPT-6 Astra completed a 50-tab tax workbook twice as fast as GPT-5.6 Sol, and its stronger understanding of user intent gives Basis more confidence in real-world use.
items.editor_note: Basis's case study: a 50-tab tax workbook finished 2x faster than with GPT-5.6 Sol, a vendor-reported comparison.

editorial.tldr: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra for coding, computer use, and long-running agentic tasks across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API by Sep 10. Perplexity's Sep 14 case study showed production monitoring delegated with far fewer check-ins, then OpenAI's Preparedness Framework rated Astra Critical for cybersecurity on Sep 17 after testers found real 0-days in a browser and an OS kernel.
editorial.whats_new: Basis became the fourth customer case study since the Critical cybersecurity rating, reporting Astra finished a 50-tab tax workbook 2x faster than GPT-5.6 Sol; still no visible new access limits.
editorial.why_it_matters: A model good enough to find real 0-days in a browser and a kernel is also good enough to weaponize them, so expect OpenAI to tighten access, logging, or usage terms around Astra's offensive-security capability rather than treating a growing run of adoption case studies as the full picture.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you're using Astra for offensive-security testing or automated vulnerability discovery, expect OpenAI to add usage restrictions or heavier logging now that it's rated Critical -- four vendor case studies since the rating haven't triggered a visible change yet, but check your API terms before the next audit cycle, not after.

status.detail: Production adoption was accelerating on trust and reduced oversight when OpenAI's Preparedness Framework classified Astra as Critical-risk for cybersecurity after it found real, previously unknown vulnerabilities; customer case studies have continued since (Higgsfield, Harvey, Basis).

beats.headline: GPT-6 Astra ships across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API
beats.summary: InfoQ confirmed availability across all three surfaces on Sep 10; OpenAI's own Sep 11 post framed it as a new generation of intelligence.

beats.headline: A 27-minute unattended run backs the long-running-task claim
beats.summary: Simon Willison had ChatGPT Work with Astra plan 5K and 10K running routes from OSM data; it ran unattended for 27 minutes and returned two accurate routes.

beats.headline: Customer trust escalates from self-testing to full delegation
beats.summary: Cognition's Devin tested its own generated code with Astra and Hex turned its analysis into shareable reports the same week; Perplexity went further, delegating production monitoring and code changes with far fewer human check-ins.

beats.headline: OpenAI classifies Astra Critical for cybersecurity after it finds real 0-days
beats.summary: Expert-led Preparedness Framework testing found previously unknown vulnerabilities in a browser and an OS kernel, making Astra the first model OpenAI has rated Critical on that axis.

beats.headline: Customer adoption keeps accelerating despite the Critical rating
beats.summary: Higgsfield shipped video ad-creation features four days after the classification, Harvey improved legal drafts, and Basis finished a 50-tab tax workbook 2x faster than GPT-5.6 Sol (a vendor-reported comparison) -- no visible new restrictions.

open_questions: Do Astra's launch-week coding and computer-use gains hold up in independent, third-party benchmarks rather than vendor case studies?
Does Perplexity's reduced check-in frequency reflect genuine reliability, or looser production guardrails that haven't yet been tested by a failure?

Nearly two weeks past the Critical classification and four case studies in, has OpenAI added any new access restrictions, usage logging, or eval requirements for API customers, and were the browser/kernel vulnerabilities disclosed and patched?
